image_description: A close-up view of a large grey whale surfacing next to a small blue boat. The whale's head and upper back are visible, showing characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. The water is choppy, and there is some text overlay at the bottom.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears somewhat consistent with a baleen whale, but the angle and resolution make it impossible to confirm the 'arched rostrum' or specifically identify 'two blowholes'. The texture looks more like rough rock or AI-generated noise than distinct biological features.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly exhibits the mottled grey/black pattern with lighter, whitish patches consistent with barnacle clusters found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the head and immediate shoulder area. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the whale is visible. The full spindle shape cannot be verified due to cropping and water occlusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the visible body section shows correct coloration and texture patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further down the body and are completely submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface has a rough, uneven texture consistent with callosities and barnacle encrustation.

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is black text overlaid on the water/boat area that is illegible and distorted, typical of AI generation failing to render coherent typography.

artifact_observations.location: Interface between whale head and water/boat
artifact_observations.reasoning: The boundary where the whale emerges from the water is slightly muddy and lacks crisp displacement physics. The connection to the blue object (boat?) on the right feels physically ambiguous and potentially fused.
While the pattern is correct, the texture has a slight 'painted' or overly smooth plastic quality in the highlights, lacking the fine micro-detail of real wet skin/barnacles.
